title: pager-trend-notes-and-canary-prep-2026-06-03
content:
Quick scratchpad for this week
Purpose: prep talking points for SRE weekly ops sync + reliability review (SLO health, recent paging trends, top incidents, canary checklist, follow-ups)

High-level summary (one-liner):
- SLOs mostly stable but token-generation latency P99 spikes on mixed-quant models during peak; page noise up 18% week-over-week driven by model-variant OOMs and auth retries in eu-west1. Need short mitigation and canary plan for upcoming rollout.

Immediate numbers to call out in sync:
- Overall error budget burn: hosted API 5.2% in 30d window (target 5%), Dedicated pools 1.1%
- Latency: text-gen P50=42ms, P95=120ms, P99=420ms (mixed-quant), target P99=350ms
- Paging events last 7d: 27 pages (baseline ~23) -> +17%
- Top page categories: GPU OOM (9), auth/token refresh failures (6), KV-cache evictions causing cold-start latency (5), routing fallbacks (4), infra flakes (3)

Top incidents to summarize (brief):
1) 2026-05-29 eu-west1-gpu-pool OOM cascade (JIRA OPS-7799)
   - Impact: ~30m elevated latency, 1 customer-facing rate limit breach for high-throughput embedder workloads.
   - Root cause: aggressive HT-concurrency + new quantized model memory regression.
   - Temp mitigation: scaled up pool by 2 nodes, enforced concurrency cap for model-families v2.
   - Follow-up: memory regression ticket to model-onboarding (assigned: Nina) ETA 6/10

2) 2026-06-01 hosted auth retry storm (JIRA OPS-7812)
   - Impact: elevated 401/429 traces and repeated retries; noisy paging between midnight-03:00 UTC.
   - Root cause: token refresh backoff misconfig on client side + spikey renewal due to clock skew in one region.
   - Follow-up: ops to push client-side SDK patch and rotate affected token issuers (assigned: Samir) ETA 6/05

SLOs + risk areas to highlight: 
- Model-variant memory regressions are single biggest risk for P99 blowups during peak. Need stronger preflight mem-sanity checks in model onboarding pipeline.
- Canary coverage gap: new quantized variants are not currently exercised by traffic mirroring; we rely on unit tests + small perf harness. Mirror path should be added to canary config for dedicated pools.

Canary / rollout checklist (for Product/Applied ML + Serving):
- [ ] Mirror 5% of production traffic to canary pool for 48h (owner: Evan)
- [ ] Add mem-usage alerts to canary with lower thresholds (owner: Nina)
- [ ] Run end-to-end latency harness for seq lengths 32/128/512 (owner: Evan)
- [ ] Validate KV-cache hitrate for canary model (owner: Samir)
- [ ] Confirm autoscaler headroom and burst policy (owner: SRE infra)

Pager trend hypotheses (brainstorm):
- H1: OOMs caused by model quantization nuance + upstream library change (lots of customers started using new variant around 5/20)
- H2: Token refresh errors amplified by a bad retry configuration + regional clock drift causing simultaneous renewals
- H3: KV-cache churn due to mis-specified prefix caching for certain chat workloads (long prompts)

Data pulls I need before sync (quick):
- 7d/30d page counts by category (CSV) -> ask SRE metrics (Samir)
- P99 latency by model-family + quantization flag -> metrics query (Evan)
- Node-level mem pressure heatmap for eu-west1 -> infra dashboard snapshot (Nina)

Unresolved questions to surface in meeting:
- Do we want automated rollback if canary P99 > baseline +15% for two consecutive 10-min windows? (ops-rollback policy)
- Is there appetite to add mirror traffic into Dedicated reserved capacity billing model? (billing implications)
- Should we temporarily tighten concurrency caps for mixed-quant models in hosted API while root cause is investigated?

Action items / owners (short):
- Nina: open model-onboarding memory regression PR + perf test updates (due 2026-06-10)
- Samir: publish 7d page category CSV + send to #sre-weekly by EOD 6/03 (DONE?)
- Evan: prototype traffic mirroring for canary pool, report feasibility by 6/05
- Avery (me): draft canary rollout proposal and rollback thresholds, share draft in #ops-sync 6/04
- SRE infra (TBD): verify autoscaler headroom and confirm burst capacity for canary (due 6/06)

Notes to self / talking points order for 10-min slot:
1) Quick numbers (SLO burn + P99 delta) 60s
2) Top pager categories + one-sentence root causes 90s
3) Canary plan ask + explicit rollback trigger 120s
4) Action items and owners 60s
5) Quick ask for required dashboards/data (Samir/Evan) 30s

Random scratch ideas:
- Could we emit a lightweight "mem-profile" event from runtime when a model's resident set increases >X% over baseline? Would help correlate pages to memory regressions faster.
- Consider a weekly small-scope canary run where we flood canary with synthetic long prompts to exercise KV-cache churn scenarios.

Local TODOs before sync (my checklist):
- [x] Pull last 30d SLO burn snapshot
- [ ] Upload canary proposal doc to Confluence and link in #ops-sync
- [ ] Slack ping Nina + Evan to confirm owners

End of scratchpad. Keep this rough; will clean up and paste top bits into meeting notes doc.
